words.ex: The angular shape of the triangle is clear.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的角形很清晰。
words.en: having angles or sharp corners; lean and bony

words.ex: He took responsibility for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了这个错误的责任。
words.en: If you have responsibility for something or someone, or if they are your responsibility, it is your job or duty to deal with them and to take decisions relating to them.

words.tr: adj. 有责任的；负责任的；
words.ex: He is responsible for cleaning the room.
words.ex_cn: 他负责打扫房间。
words.en: If someone or something is responsible for a particular event or situation, they are the cause of it or they can be blamed for it.

words.tr: adj. 易反应的；应答的；回答的；
words.ex: The child is responsive to his mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子对母亲的声音反应灵敏。
words.en: If someone or something is responsive, they react quickly and favorably.

words.tr:
n. 剩余部分；其他；休息；
v. （使）休息；（使）倚靠；停留在；
words.ex: He ate the first slice and left the rest for his sister.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了第一块，把剩下的留给了他妹妹。
words.en: To rest means to cease work or movement in order to relax, sleep, or recover strength. It can also refer to the remaining part of something.

words.ex: We ate dinner at a small restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在一家小餐厅吃了晚饭。
words.en: A restaurant is a place where you can eat a meal and pay for it. In restaurants, your food is usually served to you at your table by a waiter or waitress.

words.ex: The child was restless during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在漫长的会议中坐立不安。
words.en: If you are restless, you are unable to stay still or to be calm and happy, because you are bored or worried.

words.ex: The restoration of the old house took two years.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的修复花了两年时间。
words.en: The act of returning something to its original condition, or the state of being returned to its original condition.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.ex: The rules are too restrictive.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则太严格了。
words.en: Something that is restrictive prevents people from doing what they want to do, or from moving or acting freely.

words.tr:
n. 结果；
v. 导致；
words.ex: The result of the test was good.
words.ex_cn: 这次测试的结果很好。
words.en: A consequence, outcome, or effect of an action or situation.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.ex: He works in retail at a small store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小店从事零售工作。
words.en: The sale of goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.ex: The retailer sells clothes to customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家零售商向顾客出售衣服。
words.en: A retailer is a person or business that sells goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.ex: He retains his old photos in a box.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧照片保存在一个盒子里。
words.en: If you retain something, you keep it or continue to have it.

words.ex: He can retell the story in his own words.
words.ex_cn: 他能用自己的话复述这个故事。
words.en: To retell a story or event means to tell it again, often in a different way or with different details.

words.ex: The doctor checked his retina with a special light.
words.ex_cn: 医生用特殊的光检查了他的视网膜。
words.en: The retina is the layer at the back of the eyeball that is sensitive to light and sends signals to the brain about what is seen.

words.ex: He will retire next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将退休。
words.en: If you retire, you stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age or because you are ill.

words.ex: He plans to start his retirement next year.
words.ex_cn: 他计划明年退休。
words.en: Retirement is the period of one's life after leaving one's job and ceasing to work.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.tr:
n. 撤退；退却；静居处；
v. 撤退；退却；
words.ex: The army ordered a retreat after the battle.
words.ex_cn: 战斗后，军队下令撤退。
words.en: If you retreat, you move away from something or someone, often because you are frightened or because you want to be alone. A retreat is also a quiet, isolated place that you go to in order to rest or to do things in private.

words.tr:
n. 返回；归还；
v. 返回；归还；
words.ex: The return of the train was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 火车的返回被推迟了。
words.en: To go or come back to a place or person. To give, send, or put something back to its original place or condition.

words.ex: The family had a reunion last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 这家人上个星期天举行了团聚。
words.en: A reunion is a gathering of people who have been separated, especially members of a family or old friends, coming together again.

words.tr: v. 再结合；再统一；重聚
words.ex: The family will reunite next summer.
words.ex_cn: 这家人将在明年夏天重聚。
words.en: If people are reunited, or if someone reunites them, they meet each other again after they have been separated for some time.

words.tr: n. 再评价；重估计；货币升值
words.ex: The bank did a revaluation of the property.
words.ex_cn: 银行对房产进行了重新估价。
words.en: The act of assessing the value of something again, especially in order to increase it.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

words.tr:
n. 报复；报仇
v. 报复
words.ex: He wanted revenge for his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为他兄弟的死报仇。
words.en: Revenge involves hurting or punishing someone who has hurt or harmed you.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: The reversal of the decision made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的逆转让每个人都高兴。
words.en: A reversal is a change to an opposite direction, position, or course of action.

words.tr:
n. 反面；
v. 使倒转；（使）倒车；撤销；
words.ex: The reverse of the coin has a picture of a tree.
words.ex_cn: 硬币的反面有一棵树的图案。
words.en: If you reverse the order of a set of things, you arrange them in the opposite order, so that the first thing comes last.

words.ex: The change is reversible under normal conditions.
words.ex_cn: 在正常条件下，这种变化是可逆的。
words.en: Capable of being reversed; able to return to an original state or condition.

words.tr:
n. 回顾；复习；审查；评论；
v. 回顾；复习；审核；评论；
words.ex: We had a quick review of last week's lesson.
words.ex_cn: 我们对上周的课程做了一个简短的回顾。
words.en: If you review something, you consider it again, especially in order to make changes to it or to give your opinion about it.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: He did revision for his math test last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚为数学考试进行了复习。
words.en: The act or process of revising; a revised or new version, as of a book or other written material.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

words.ex: The revival of traditional music brought joy to many people.
words.ex_cn: 传统音乐的复兴给许多人带来了快乐。
words.en: The process of something becoming popular or active again after a period of inactivity or decline.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.tr: v. 使复活；使苏醒；使有生气；使恢复精神
words.ex: The old song revivifies my memories.
words.ex_cn: 那首老歌唤起了我的回忆。
words.en: To bring something back to life, to make it lively or vigorous again.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.ex: The French Revolution changed the government.
words.ex_cn: 法国大革命改变了政府。
words.en: A revolution is a sudden, extreme, or complete change in something, or the act of making such a change.

words.ex: The revolutionary idea changed the world.
words.ex_cn: 这个革命性的想法改变了世界。
words.en: Involving or causing a complete or dramatic change.

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

words.ex: He held a revolver in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他手里拿着一把左轮手枪。
words.en: A revolver is a handgun that has a cylinder with several chambers, each capable of holding a cartridge, and that can be fired repeatedly without reloading by rotating the cylinder to align a new chamber with the barrel.

words.tr:
n. 奖励；报酬；
v. 奖励；回报；
words.ex: He got a reward for winning the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得比赛而得到了奖励。
words.en: Something given or received in return for a deed or service rendered.

words.ex: He had to rewrite his essay after the teacher gave feedback.
words.ex_cn: 他在老师给出反馈后不得不重写他的作文。
words.en: If someone rewrites a piece of writing such as a book, an article, or a law, they write it in a different way in order to improve it or because circumstances have changed.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.tr: adj. 修辞性的；词藻华丽的；反问的
words.ex: He asked a rhetorical question to make a point.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个修辞性的问题来阐明观点。
words.en: A rhetorical question is one which is asked in order to make a statement rather than to get an answer.

words.ex: She suffered from rheumatism in her joints.
words.ex_cn: 她的关节患有风湿病。
words.en: Rheumatism is any disease marked by inflammation and pain in the joints, muscles, or fibrous tissue, especially rheumatoid arthritis.

words.ex: The rhino is walking in the grass.
words.ex_cn: 犀牛正在草地上行走。
words.en: A rhinoceros, often abbreviated to rhino, is one of any five extant species of odd-toed ungulates in the family Rhinocerotidae, as well as any of the numerous extinct species.

words.tr:
n. 韵文；
v. 押韵；
words.ex: The poem has a simple rhyme.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有一段简单的韵文。
words.en: A rhyme is a repetition of similar sounds in the final stressed syllables and any following syllables of two or more words, most often used in poetry.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.tr: adj. 有节奏的；有韵律的；
words.ex: The children danced to the rhythmic beat.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们随着有节奏的节拍跳舞。
words.en: A rhythmic sound or movement has a clear and regular pattern that is repeated.

words.tr: adj. 有节奏的；有韵律的（=rhythmic）
words.ex: The drum beats are rhythmical and loud.
words.ex_cn: 鼓点有节奏且响亮。
words.en: Having a regular repeated pattern of sounds or movements.

words.ex: He hurt his rib when he fell.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒时伤到了肋骨。
words.en: A rib is one of the long curved bones that are connected to the spine and surround the chest.

words.ex: She tied a red ribbon around the box.
words.ex_cn: 她把一条红色的带状物系在盒子上。
words.en: A ribbon is a long, narrow piece of cloth that you use for tying things together or as a decoration.

words.ex: He eats rice every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃米饭。
words.en: Rice is a cereal grain that is the most widely consumed staple food for a large part of the world's human population, especially in Asia.

words.tr: adj. 丰饶的；富有的；富裕的；
words.ex: The land is rich in minerals.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地矿物丰富。
words.en: Having a great deal of money or assets; wealthy.

words.ex: He wants to rid his house of clutter.
words.ex_cn: 他想摆脱家里的杂乱。
words.en: To rid someone or something of something unwanted or harmful means to remove it completely from them.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.tr:
n. 骑；乘坐；
v. 骑；乘坐；
words.ex: He gave me a ride on his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他让我骑了他的自行车。
words.en: To sit on and control the movement of an animal, especially a horse, or to travel in or on a vehicle or other conveyance.

words.ex: The bridge crosses the river.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥横跨河流。
words.en: A bridge is a structure that is built over a railway, river, or road so that people or vehicles can cross from one side to the other.

words.ex: He faced ridicule for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他因为穿旧衣服而遭到嘲笑。
words.en: To ridicule someone or something means to make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.ex: It's ridiculous to think he can run a mile in one minute.
words.ex_cn: 认为他能在一分钟内跑完一英里是荒谬的。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is ridiculous, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.tr:
n. 步枪；来复枪（又称来福枪）
v. 快速搜寻
words.ex: He carries a rifle in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他带着一把步枪在森林里。
words.en: A rifle is a gun with a long barrel which you hold against your shoulder when firing.

words.ex: The rifleman took aim and fired.
words.ex_cn: 步枪兵瞄准并开火。
words.en: A rifleman is a soldier who is skilled in the use of a rifle.

words.tr:
adv. 正确地；直接地；向右；
adj. 正确的；右边的；
n. 右边；权利；
v. 纠正；
words.ex: He answered the question right.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地回答了问题。
words.en: If something is right, it is correct and agrees with the facts.

words.tr: adj. 右手的；右侧的；用右手做的；得力的
words.ex: He writes with his right-hand side.
words.ex_cn: 他用右手写字。
words.en: The right-hand side or part of something is the side or part that is towards the right.

words.ex: He rightly answered the question.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地回答了这个问题。
words.en: If you say that someone rightly does something, you mean that it is morally or legally correct for them to do it.

words.ex: He supports right-wing policies.
words.ex_cn: 他支持右翼政策。
words.en: The right-wing of a political party or system is the part of it that generally opposes socialism and favors private property and capitalism.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.tr:
v. 给…打电话；响铃；
n. 环；环形物；铃声；拳击场；
words.ex: I will ring you tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天给你打电话。
words.en: A ring is a small circular band, typically of precious metal and often set with one or more gemstones, worn on a finger as an ornament or a token of marriage, engagement, or authority. It can also refer to the act of making a clear resonant or vibrating sound, or to encircle or surround something.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.ex: The child ripped the paper with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用手把纸撕裂了。
words.en: To rip something means to tear it quickly and forcefully.

words.ex: The apple is ripe and ready to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果熟了，可以吃了。
words.en: When fruit or crops are ripe, they are ready to be eaten or harvested because they have developed to the right stage.

words.ex: The apples ripen in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 苹果在秋天成熟。
words.en: When crops ripen or when the sun ripens them, they become ripe and ready to eat.

words.tr:
v. （使）成波浪状；（使）起涟漪；作潺潺声 
n. 微波；涟漪；潺潺声
words.ex: The wind ripples the surface of the lake.
words.ex_cn: 风使湖面泛起波浪。
words.en: If something ripples, it moves in small waves or if you ripple it, you make it move in small waves.

words.tr:
n. 上升；提高；
v. 上升；提高；
words.ex: There was a rise in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度上升了。
words.en: If an amount or level rises, it increases; if something rises, it moves upwards; if you rise, you stand up; if you rise, you get out of bed.

words.tr:
n. 风险；
v. 冒...的危险；
words.ex: He took a risk by starting his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他创业时承担了风险。
words.en: If there is a risk of something unpleasant, there is a possibility that it will happen.

words.ex: It's risky to walk alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 晚上独自走路是危险的。
words.en: If an activity or action is risky, it is dangerous or likely to fail.

words.ex: He writes a letter every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写一封信。
words.en: To write means to form letters, words, or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.tr:
n. 竞争者；敌手；
v. 竞争；相匹敌；
words.ex: He is my main rival in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他是我在比赛中主要的竞争者。
words.en: A rival is a person, group, or organization that you are competing with in the same activity or the same area.

words.ex: The rivalry between the two teams is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍之间的竞争非常激烈。
words.en: Competition for the same objective or for superiority in the same field.

words.ex: The children play near the river.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在河边玩耍。
words.en: A river is a large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another river.

words.ex: The road is long and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 这条路又长又安静。
words.en: A road is a long piece of hard ground which is built between two places so that people can drive or ride easily from one place to the other.

words.ex: He picked up some flowers from the roadside.
words.ex_cn: 他从路边摘了一些花。
words.en: The edge of a road, especially a country road, where people can park or walk.

words.ex: The children played on the roadway.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在道路上玩耍。
words.en: The part of a road intended for vehicles to travel on.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.tr:
v. 吼叫；咆哮
n. 吼叫；咆哮
words.ex: The lion let out a loud roar.
words.ex_cn: 狮子发出了一声响亮的咆哮。
words.en: If something roars, it makes a very loud noise, like the sound of a lion.

words.tr:
n. 烤肉；烘烤；
adj. 烤的；焙的；
v. 烤；烘烤；
words.ex: We had roast for dinner last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚我们吃了烤肉。
words.en: To cook food, such as meat, in an oven or over a fire.

words.ex: The thieves robbed the bank last night.
words.ex_cn: 小偷昨晚抢劫了银行。
words.en: To rob someone or somewhere means to take money or property illegally from them, often using force.

words.ex: The robbery happened at the bank yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天银行发生了抢劫。
words.en: The crime of stealing from someone or somewhere, especially using violence or threats.

words.tr:
n. 长袍
v. （使）穿上长袍
words.ex: He puts on a white robe after the shower.
words.ex_cn: 他洗完澡后穿上一件白袍。
words.en: A robe is a long, loose piece of clothing that covers all of your body and reaches the ground. It is often worn for ceremonies or in the home.

words.ex: The robin sang loudly in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 知更鸟在早晨大声歌唱。
words.en: A small bird with a red breast, known for its melodious song.

words.ex: The robot cleans the floor every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人每天打扫地板。
words.en: A robot is a machine that is programmed to move and perform certain tasks automatically.

words.tr:
n. 岩石；摇滚乐；
v. （使）摇动；（使）摇晃；
words.ex: The children climbed on the big rock near the river.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在河边的大岩石上攀爬。
words.en: A rock is a large piece of stone that forms part of a hill or mountain. Rock can also refer to a type of music that is loud and has a strong beat. As a verb, to rock means to move gently backwards and forwards or from side to side.

words.ex: The rocket flew into space.
words.ex_cn: 火箭飞入了太空。
words.en: A rocket is a spacecraft, aircraft, or other vehicle that obtains thrust from a rocket engine.

words.ex: The rocky path made hiking difficult.
words.ex_cn: 多岩石的小路让徒步变得困难。
words.en: A rocky area is covered with rocks or consists of large areas of rock and has nothing growing on it.

words.ex: He used a long rod to reach the top shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根长杆够到顶层架子。
words.en: A rod is a long, thin, straight bar, especially one made of wood or metal.

words.ex: He played the role of a teacher in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他在电影中扮演了老师的角色。
words.en: The function or position that someone has in a particular situation or activity.

words.tr:
v. 滚动；
n. 滚动；卷形物；
words.ex: The ball roll down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 球从山上滚下来。
words.en: To move somewhere by turning over and over, or to make something move in this way.

words.ex: The painter used a roller to apply the paint.
words.ex_cn: 油漆工用滚筒来涂油漆。
words.en: A roller is a cylinder that rotates around a central axis and is used in various machines and devices to move, flatten, or compress something.

words.ex: She used a rolling-pin to flatten the dough.
words.ex_cn: 她用擀面杖把面团擀平。
words.en: A rolling-pin is a cylinder that you roll backwards and forwards over uncooked pastry or dough in order to make it flat.

words.tr:
adj. 古罗马的；罗马人的；
n. 古罗马人；
words.ex: The ancient roman roads are still visible today.
words.ex_cn: 古老的罗马道路至今仍清晰可见。
words.en: A Roman is a person who comes from Rome or is connected with Rome. It can also refer to the style of printing or writing that uses upright letters, as opposed to italic.

words.ex: They wrote a love letter every day, and it became their romance.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天写一封情书，这成为了他们的浪漫史。
words.en: Romance refers to the feelings and behaviors characteristic of love, especially in its early stages, or a story, movie, or other work dealing with love in a sentimental or idealized way.

words.ex: He gave her a romantic gift on Valentine's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他在情人节送了她一份浪漫的礼物。
words.en: If you describe something as romantic, you mean that it is connected with love or with a feeling of excitement and mystery associated with love.

words.ex: He loves romanticism in old poems.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢旧诗歌中的浪漫主义。
words.en: Romanticism is a movement in the arts and literature which originated in the late 18th century, emphasizing inspiration, subjectivity, and the primacy of the individual.

words.tr:
n. 铬；铬合金；铬黄
v. 镀以铬
words.ex: Chrome is a metal used in car parts.
words.ex_cn: 铬是一种用于汽车零件的金属。
words.en: Chrome is a hard, shiny metal that is used to cover other metals to prevent them from rusting and to make them look more attractive.

words.ex: The cat sat on the roof.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在屋顶上。
words.en: The roof of a building is the covering on top of it that protects the people and things inside from the weather.

words.ex: The room has a bed and a window.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有一张床和一扇窗户。
words.en: A room is a part of the inside of a building that is separated from other parts by walls, floor, and ceiling.

words.tr:
n. 根；根源；
v. 生根；
words.ex: The root of 9 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 9的平方根是3。
words.en: The root of a plant is the part that grows underground and absorbs water and minerals. It can also refer to the origin or cause of something.

words.ex: He tied the box with a strong rope.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根结实的绳子把箱子绑了起来。
words.en: A rope is a thick cord made by twisting together strands of natural fibers such as hemp or artificial fibers such as nylon.

words.tr: n. 玫瑰； v. 上升；提高；“rise”的过去式；
words.ex: She picked a red rose from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她从花园里摘了一朵红玫瑰。
words.en: A rose is a flower, often with a pleasant smell, which grows on a bush with thorns on the stems.

words.tr: adj. 玫瑰色的；红润的（皮肤）；美好的；有希望的（前途等）
words.ex: The sky turned rosy at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 日出时，天空变成了玫瑰色。
words.en: If you describe a situation as rosy, you mean that it seems to be full of hope and promise.

words.ex: The rotary switch turns on the light.
words.ex_cn: 旋转开关打开灯。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by rotation.

words.ex: The wheel rotates slowly.
words.ex_cn: 轮子缓慢地转动。
words.en: To rotate means to turn or cause to turn around an axis or center.

words.ex: The students have a rotational schedule for cleaning the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 学生们轮流负责打扫教室。
words.en: Relating to or involving rotation; occurring in turn or sequence.

words.ex: The apple is rotten and smells bad.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果腐烂了，闻起来很难闻。
words.en: Something that is rotten has decayed and cannot be used for its normal purpose.

words.ex: The wood surface is rough.
words.ex_cn: 木头表面很粗糙。
words.en: If a surface is rough, it is not smooth and has bumps or uneven areas.

words.ex: There are roughly 100 students in the class.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级大约有100名学生。
words.en: In a manner that is not exact or detailed; approximately.

words.tr:
prep. 在…周围；环绕；
adv. 环绕；附近；
adj. 圆的；十足的；
n. 回合；圆形物；
v. 拐过；使成圆形；
words.ex: The children sat round the fire.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们围坐在火堆旁。
words.en: Something that is round is shaped like a circle or a ball.

words.ex: The car turned at the roundabout near the park.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在公园附近的环形交叉路口转弯。
words.en: A roundabout is a circular area at a place where several roads meet. You drive round it until you come to the road that you want.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

words.tr:
n. 常规；例行公事；
adj. 常规的；例行公事的；
words.ex: He follows a morning routine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都遵循固定的惯例。
words.en: A routine is a sequence of actions regularly followed; a fixed program.

words.ex: The students sat in a row.
words.ex_cn: 学生们坐成一排。
words.en: A row is a straight line of things or people. To row means to move a boat through water using oars.

words.ex: The rower practices every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这位划船运动员每天早上练习。
words.en: A person who rows a boat, especially in a race or as a sport.

words.ex: The royal family lives in a big palace.
words.ex_cn: 皇室住在一座大宫殿里。
words.en: Royal is used to describe something that is connected with a king, queen, or emperor, or with their family. It can also describe something that is splendid or magnificent, befitting a king or queen.

words.ex: The royalty lived in a large palace.
words.ex_cn: 皇族住在一座大宫殿里。
words.en: Royalty refers to people of royal blood or status, or a sum of money paid to an author, composer, etc., for each copy of a work sold or for each public performance of their work.

words.ex: He rubs his hands together to warm them.
words.ex_cn: 他搓手来暖和它们。
words.en: To move one's hand or a cloth repeatedly back and forth on the surface of something with firm pressure.

words.ex: The boy picked up a piece of rubber from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 男孩从地上捡起一块橡胶。
words.en: Rubber is a strong, waterproof, elastic substance made from the juice of some tropical plants or artificially. It is used for making tires, boots, and many other products.

words.ex: He threw the rubbish into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: Waste material; refuse or litter.

words.ex: She wears a ruby ring on her finger.
words.ex_cn: 她手指上戴着一枚红宝石戒指。
words.en: A ruby is a precious stone that is typically a deep red color.

words.ex: He was rude to the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 他对服务员很无礼。
words.en: If someone is rude, they behave in a way that is not polite and upsets other people.

words.ex: He sat on the rug near the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在壁炉旁的地毯上。
words.en: A rug is a piece of thick material that you put on the floor to cover part of it and to make it warmer or softer to walk on.

words.ex: He plays rugby every Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 他每个星期六打橄榄球。
words.en: Rugby is a sport played by two teams of 15 players each, using an oval ball that players kick, pass, or carry in order to score points by grounding the ball behind the opponent's goal line or kicking it between the goalposts.

words.ex: The hikers walked on a rugged trail.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走在一条崎岖的小路上。
words.en: A rugged area of land is uneven and covered with rocks, with few trees or plants.

words.tr:
n. 废墟；
v. 破坏；
words.ex: The old temple is now a ruin.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙现在已成为废墟。
words.en: Ruin means the physical destruction or disintegration of something or the state of disintegrating or being destroyed.

words.tr:
n. 规则；统治；
v. 统治；
words.ex: The teacher made a new rule for homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师制定了一个新的作业规则。
words.en: A rule is a statement telling people what they should do in order to achieve success or a benefit of some kind.

words.ex: The ruler made laws for his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者为他的人民制定法律。
words.en: A ruler is a person who governs or commands. It can also refer to a straight strip or cylinder of plastic, wood, metal, or other rigid material, typically marked at regular intervals and used to draw straight lines or measure distances.

words.tr:
n. 谣言
v. 谣传
words.ex: There is a rumour that he will quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 有一个传言说他要辞职。
words.en: A rumour is a story or piece of information that may or may not be true, but that people are talking about.

words.tr:
n. 谣言
v. 谣传
words.ex: The rumor spread quickly that the school would close.
words.ex_cn: 学校即将关闭的谣言迅速传播开来。
words.en: A rumor is a story or piece of information that may or may not be true, but that people are talking about.

words.tr:
v. 经营；跑步；
n. 运转；跑；
words.ex: He runs a small coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他经营一家小咖啡馆。
words.en: To move quickly on foot so that both feet leave the ground during each stride.

words.tr: adj. 失控的；物价飞涨的；
words.ex: The runaway train crashed into the station.
words.ex_cn: 这列失控的火车撞上了车站。
words.en: A runaway is someone who has run away from home or an institution, or something that is out of control and moving or acting without being directed.

words.ex: The runner won the race quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这位跑步者很快赢得了比赛。
words.en: A runner is a person who runs, especially in a race or as a sport.

words.ex: He was the runner-up in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中获得了亚军。
words.en: A runner-up is someone who finishes in second place in a competition.

words.tr: n. 跑；管理；运作； v. 经营；跑步；“run”的现在分词； adj. 运作中的；流动的；持续的；
words.ex: Running is his favorite exercise.
words.ex_cn: 跑步是他最喜欢的锻炼方式。
words.en: The act of moving swiftly on foot so that both feet leave the ground during each stride.

words.ex: The plane landed on the runway.
words.ex_cn: 飞机降落在跑道上。
words.en: A runway is a strip of land where aircraft take off and land.

words.ex: He lives in a rural village with no big shops.
words.ex_cn: 他住在没有大商店的农村村庄里。
words.en: Rural areas are areas which are not towns or cities. They are often farming or agricultural areas.

words.tr:
n. 冲；匆忙；
v. 冲；赶忙做；
words.ex: There was a rush to buy tickets for the concert.
words.ex_cn: 人们争相购买演唱会的票。
words.en: If you rush somewhere, you go there quickly. A rush is a situation in which you need to go somewhere or do something very quickly.

words.tr:
adj. 俄国的；
n. 俄语；
words.ex: He loves Russian music and food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢俄罗斯的音乐和食物。
words.en: Relating to Russia, its people, or their language.

words.ex: The old bike has rust on its chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条上有锈。
words.en: Rust is a reddish-brown substance that forms on the surface of iron or steel when they are exposed to air and moisture, causing them to corrode.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.ex: The old bike has a rusty chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条生锈了。
words.en: If something is rusty, it is covered with rust or has become less good because it has not been used for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 无情的；冷酷的；残忍的；
words.ex: The ruthless boss fired employees without warning.
words.ex_cn: 这位无情的老板未经警告就解雇了员工。
words.en: If you say that someone is ruthless, you mean that you disapprove of them because they are very harsh or cruel, and will do anything that is necessary to achieve what they want.

words.ex: He ate bread made from rye.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了用黑麦做的面包。
words.en: Rye is a type of cereal plant grown in cool climates. It is used for making bread, whiskey, and animal feed.

words.tr:
n. 袋子；
v. 劫掠；
words.ex: He carried the apples in a burlap sack.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果装在一个麻布袋里。
words.en: A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material, used for storing or carrying goods. It can also refer to the act of dismissing someone from employment or the act of looting a place.

words.tr:
n. 麻袋布；粗麻布；解雇；开除
v. 解雇；装入袋子；劫掠；“sack”的现在分词
words.ex: The boss is angry and thinks about sacking the worker.
words.ex_cn: 老板很生气，正在考虑解雇那个工人。
words.en: The act of dismissing someone from employment; a coarse fabric woven from flax or hemp.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.ex: He felt sad when his dog ran away.
words.ex_cn: 当他的狗跑掉时，他感到伤心。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow; unhappy.

words.ex: The news saddened her.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让她感到悲伤。
words.en: If something saddens you, it makes you feel sad.

words.tr:
n. 马鞍；鞍座
v. 给（马）装鞍
words.ex: The boy rode on a saddle on the horse.
words.ex_cn: 男孩骑在马的马鞍上。
words.en: A saddle is a seat for a rider on the back of a horse or other animal, or a similar seat on a bicycle or motorcycle. It can also refer to the act of putting a saddle on a horse or to burden someone with a responsibility.

words.ex: He felt sadness after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他失去狗后感到悲伤。
words.en: Sadness is the feeling of being unhappy, especially because something bad has happened.

words.ex: The children are playing in a safe park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在安全的公园里玩耍。
words.en: If something or someone is safe, they are not in danger or likely to be harmed.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet improves your safety.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔能提高你的安全。
words.en: Safety refers to the condition of being protected from or unlikely to cause danger, risk, or injury.

words.tr:
v. 航行；驾（船）；
n. 帆；航行；航海；
words.ex: They sail to the island every summer.
words.ex_cn: 他们每年夏天都乘船航行到那个岛。
words.en: To sail means to travel on water in a ship or boat, especially one that uses sails to catch the wind.

words.ex: The sailor fixed the rope on the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手修理了船上的绳子。
words.en: A sailor is a person who works on a ship as a member of its crew.

words.ex: Saint Francis loved animals and helped the poor.
words.ex_cn: 圣方济各热爱动物并帮助穷人。
words.en: A saint is a person who is recognized as having an exceptional degree of holiness, likeness, or closeness to God.

words.ex: He did it for her sake.
words.ex_cn: 他为了她的缘故做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something for the sake of something, you do it for that purpose or in order to achieve that result. You can also say that you do it for something's sake.

words.ex: I ate a fresh salad for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 我午餐吃了一份新鲜的色拉。
words.en: A salad is a mixture of raw vegetables such as lettuce, cucumber, and tomatoes, often served with a dressing.

words.ex: He gets a salary of 3000 dollars each month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月赚3000美元的工资。
words.en: A salary is the money that someone is paid each month by their employer, especially when they are in a profession such as teaching, law, or medicine.

words.tr: n. 销售；出售；减价销售；
words.ex: The store has a big sale every winter.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店每年冬天都有大促销。
words.en: The exchange of a commodity for money; the action of selling something.

words.ex: The salesclerk helped the customer find the right size.
words.ex_cn: 售货员帮助顾客找到了合适的尺码。
words.en: A salesclerk is a person whose job is to serve customers in a store.

words.tr: n. 女售货员；女营业员
words.ex: The salesgirl helped me find a red dress.
words.ex_cn: 女售货员帮我找到了一件红色连衣裙。
words.en: A salesgirl is a young woman whose job is to sell goods in a shop.

words.ex: The saleslady was very helpful in finding the right size for me.
words.ex_cn: 那位女售货员非常热心地帮我找到了合适的尺码。
words.en: A saleslady is a woman whose job is to sell goods in a shop.

words.tr: n. 男推销员；男售货员；
words.ex: The salesman showed us new phones.
words.ex_cn: 那位男推销员给我们展示了新手机。
words.en: A salesman is a man whose job is to sell things, especially directly to shops or other businesses on behalf of a company.

words.ex: He is a sales manager at a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他是家小公司的销售经理。
words.en: A sales manager is a person who is responsible for leading and guiding a team of sales people in an organization. They set sales goals, analyze data, and develop training programs for sales representatives.

words.ex: Dogs produce saliva when they smell food.
words.ex_cn: 狗闻到食物时会分泌唾液。
words.en: Saliva is the watery liquid that forms in your mouth and helps you to chew and digest food.

words.tr: n. 鲑鱼；三文鱼；大马哈鱼；
words.ex: He grilled salmon for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他烤了鲑鱼当晚餐。
words.en: A salmon is a large silver-coloured fish which lives in the sea and rivers.

words.tr: n. 美容院；美发厅；沙龙
words.ex: She goes to the salon to get her hair cut.
words.ex_cn: 她去理发店剪头发。
words.en: A salon is a gathering of people under the roof of an inspiring host, held partly to amuse one another and partly to refine the taste and increase the knowledge of the participants through conversation.

words.ex: They met at a saloon to discuss art and music.
words.ex_cn: 他们在一个沙龙里讨论艺术和音乐。
words.en: A saloon is a public room or building used for a specified purpose, especially a bar in the western U.S. in the 19th century.

words.ex: She added a little salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她在汤里加了一点盐。
words.en: Salt is a white crystalline substance that is used for seasoning or preserving food. It is also used in various industrial processes.

words.ex: The soup is too salty.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太咸了。
words.en: Something that is salty contains salt or tastes of salt.

words.tr:
n. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
v. 敬礼；致敬；行礼
words.ex: The soldier gave a salute to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 士兵向军官敬礼。
words.en: If you salute someone, you greet them or show your respect with a formal sign. Soldiers usually salute officers by raising their right hand so that their fingers touch their forehead.

words.ex: The firefighters brought salvation to the people trapped in the burning building.
words.ex_cn: 消防员拯救了被困在着火大楼里的人们。
words.en: Salvation is the act of saving or protecting from harm, risk, loss, destruction, etc., or the state of being saved from such conditions.

words.ex: He has the same book as me.
words.ex_cn: 他有一本和我一样的书。
words.en: If two or more things, actions, or qualities are the same, or if one is the same as another, they are very like each other in some way.

words.ex: The fisherman rowed his sampan through the narrow canals.
words.ex_cn: 渔夫划着他的舢板穿过狭窄的运河。
words.en: A sampan is a relatively flat-bottomed Chinese wooden boat. Some sampans include a small shelter on board and may be used as a permanent habitation on inland waters.

words.tr:
n. 样品；样本；
v. 抽样；
words.ex: The scientist tested the sample from the river.
words.ex_cn: 科学家测试了来自河流的样品。
words.en: A sample is a small quantity of a product, especially food, given to customers so that they can try it before buying it.

words.ex: He went to the sanatorium to rest and get better.
words.ex_cn: 他去疗养院休息并康复。
words.en: A sanatorium is an institution for the medical treatment and recuperation of people who are chronically ill.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.ex: The children built a castle in the sand.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在沙子里建了一座城堡。
words.en: Sand is a substance that consists of very small grains of rock, found on beaches and in deserts.

words.ex: She wore sandals to the beach.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着凉鞋去海滩。
words.en: A sandal is a type of light shoe that you wear in warm weather, which has straps that go over your foot and around your ankle.

words.ex: The old castle is built from red sandstone.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡是用红色砂岩建造的。
words.en: Sandstone is a type of sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized minerals or rock grains.

words.ex: He eats a sandwich for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃三明治。
words.en: A sandwich consists of two slices of bread with a layer of food such as cheese or meat between them.

words.ex: The beach has sandy soil.
words.ex_cn: 这个海滩有含沙的土壤。
words.en: Covered with or consisting mostly of sand.

words.tr: adj. 心智健全的；头脑清醒的；明智的
words.ex: He is still sane after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他仍然神志清醒。
words.en: If someone is sane, they are able to think and behave in a normal and rational manner.

words.tr: adj. 血淋淋的；嗜杀的；残暴的
words.ex: The battle was known for its sanguinary nature.
words.ex_cn: 这场战斗因其血腥的性质而闻名。
words.en: Involving or causing much bloodshed; marked by great slaughter.

words.ex: The kitchen must be sanitary to prevent illness.
words.ex_cn: 厨房必须保持清洁以防止疾病。
words.en: relating to the conditions that affect hygiene and health, especially the supply of sewage facilities and clean drinking water

words.tr: n. 心智健全；神志清楚；神智健全
words.ex: The doctors questioned his sanity after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，医生们质疑他的精神是否健全。
words.en: The condition of having a healthy mind and not being mentally ill.

words.ex: Santa Claus brings gifts on Christmas Eve.
words.ex_cn: 圣诞老人在平安夜送礼物。
words.en: Santa Claus is a legendary figure originating in Western Christian culture who is said to bring gifts to the homes of well-behaved children on Christmas Eve.

words.tr:
n. 树液；
v. 使逐渐耗竭；使削弱；
words.ex: The tree releases sap in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在春天流出树液。
words.en: Sap is the watery fluid that circulates in the vascular system of a plant, carrying nutrients and sugars. It can also refer to the vitality or energy of a person or thing.

words.ex: He planted a sapling in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 他在后院种了一棵树苗。
words.en: A sapling is a young tree.

words.ex: He said it with sarcasm, even though he seemed happy.
words.ex_cn: 他说这话时带着讽刺，尽管他看起来很高兴。
words.en: Sarcasm is a sharp, bitter, or cutting expression or remark; a bitter gibe or taunt.

words.tr: adj. 讽刺的；嘲讽的；挖苦的
words.ex: He gave a sarcastic laugh when she said she was perfect.
words.ex_cn: 当她说自己完美时，他讽刺地笑了一声。
words.en: If you describe someone as sarcastic, you mean that they are inclined to say things which are the opposite of what they really mean, especially in order to mock or insult someone.

words.tr: n. 沙丁鱼；沙丁鱼罐头
words.ex: He ate a sardine for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一条沙丁鱼。
words.en: A small fish that is often canned and eaten as food.

words.ex: Satan is often depicted as a fallen angel.
words.ex_cn: 撒旦常被描绘成一个堕落的天使。
words.en: In Christian belief, Satan is the Devil, the main spirit of evil, who tries to make people do bad things.

words.ex: He carries a brown satchel to school.
words.ex_cn: 他背着一个棕色的书包去学校。
words.en: A satchel is a bag with a long strap, traditionally used for carrying books.

words.ex: The satellite sends pictures from space.
words.ex_cn: 卫星从太空发送图片。
words.en: A satellite is an object which has been sent into space in order to collect information or to be part of a communications system. Satellites move continually round the earth or around another planet.

words.tr:
n. 缎子；缎子衣服
adj. 缎子似的；平滑而有光泽的
v. 对（纸等）作加光处理
words.ex: She wore a dress made of satin.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件缎子做的衣服。
words.en: Satin is a type of cloth that is smooth and shiny on one side and dull on the other.

words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.ex: The cartoon is satirical and makes fun of politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画是讽刺性的，嘲笑政客。
words.en: A satirical piece of writing or speech uses satire to criticize people or ideas.

words.ex: The play satirises the political corruption.
words.ex_cn: v. 这部戏剧讽刺了政治腐败。
words.en: To satirise means to use satire to criticize or mock someone or something.

words.ex: The cartoon satirizes politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画讽刺了政治家。
words.en: If you satirize a person or group of people, you use satire to criticize them or make fun of them in a play, movie, or novel.

words.ex: The satirist made fun of the president in his show.
words.ex_cn: 这位讽刺作家在他的节目中嘲笑那位总统。
words.en: A satirist is someone who writes or uses satire.

words.ex: He felt satisfaction after finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他完成作业后感到满意。
words.en: The feeling of pleasure that you have when you do or get something that you wanted or needed.

words.ex: The teacher gave a satisfactory grade.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个令人满意的分数。
words.en: If something is satisfactory, it is good enough or acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 满意的；满足的； v. 使满意；使满足；“satisfy”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was satisfied with the result.
words.ex_cn: 他对结果感到满意。
words.en: If you are satisfied with something, you are happy because you have got what you wanted or needed.

words.ex: The teacher gave extra praise to satisfy the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给予额外的表扬来使学生满意。
words.en: If someone or something satisfies you, they give you enough of what you want or need to make you pleased or contented.

words.ex: Saturn has beautiful rings around it.
words.ex_cn: 土星周围有美丽的光环。
words.en: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun in the Solar System and is known for its prominent ring system, which is composed mainly of ice particles with a smaller amount of rocky debris and dust.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: We go to the park on Saturday.
words.ex_cn: 我们在星期六去公园。
words.en: Saturday is the day of the week that comes after Friday and before Sunday.

words.ex: He poured sauce on his pasta.
words.ex_cn: 他把酱汁倒在意大利面上。
words.en: A sauce is a thick liquid which is served with other food.

words.ex: She boiled water in a saucepan.
words.ex_cn: 她用锅烧水。
words.en: A saucepan is a deep cooking pan, typically round, made of metal, and with a long handle and a lid.

words.ex: He put the cup on a saucer.
words.ex_cn: 他把杯子放在一个茶托上。
words.en: A small shallow dish, typically circular, on which a cup is placed.

words.tr: n. 桑拿浴室；桑拿浴；蒸汽浴
words.ex: He relaxes in the sauna after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后在桑拿房里放松。
words.en: A sauna is a small room used as a hot-air or steam bath for cleaning and refreshing the body.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；漫步
n. 闲逛；漫步
words.ex: We decided to saunter along the beach.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定沿着海滩漫步。
words.en: If you saunter somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: He ate a sausage for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一根香肠。
words.en: A sausage is a type of meat product usually made from ground meat, often pork, beef, or poultry, along with salt, spices, and other flavorings. Other ingredients such as grains or breadcrumbs may be included as fillers or extenders.

words.ex: The savage wolf howled under the moon.
words.ex_cn: 那头野性的狼在月光下嚎叫。
words.en: A savage person or animal is very fierce and violent.

words.tr:
v. 节省；拯救；保存；
prep. 除...之外；除了；
words.ex: He saves money by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省钱。
words.en: To save something means to keep it from being lost or damaged; to save money or time is to avoid spending more than necessary.

words.tr: n. 储蓄金；存款；“saving”的复数；
words.ex: He used his savings to buy a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他用他的储蓄买了一辆新自行车。
words.en: Money that someone has saved, especially in a bank or official scheme.

words.tr: n. 救星；救主；拯救者；救助者
words.ex: She was seen as a saviour by many in the community.
words.ex_cn: 她在社区里被许多人视为救星。
words.en: A saviour is a person who saves someone or something from danger, harm, or failure.

words.ex: The firefighters were hailed as saviors for their heroic efforts.
words.ex_cn: 消防员们因他们的英勇努力而被赞誉为救星。
words.en: A savior is a person who saves someone or something from danger, harm, or failure.

words.tr:
adj. 咸的；香辣的；香喷喷的；风味极佳的；舒适宜人的；体面的；名声好的
n. （烹饪调味的）香薄荷；使人开胃的菜肴
words.ex: The soup is savoury and delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这汤咸香可口。
words.en: Savoury food is salty or spicy and not sweet in taste.

words.ex: I saw a bird fly over the house.
words.ex_cn: 我看到一只鸟飞过房子。
words.en: A saw is a tool consisting of a tough blade, wire, or chain with a hard toothed edge. It is used to cut through material, very often wood, though sometimes metal or stone. The cut is made by placing the toothed edge against the material and moving it forcefully forth and less forcefully back or continuously forward.

words.ex: The sawmill processes logs into lumber.
words.ex_cn: 锯木厂将原木加工成木材。
words.en: A sawmill is a factory where logs are cut into boards.

words.ex: He says hello every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都说你好。
words.en: To express in words; to state or declare.

words.tr: v. “say”的现在分词；说； n. 谚语；警句；
words.ex: He is saying goodbye to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他正在向朋友们道别。
words.en: A short, well-known expression that states a general truth or gives advice.

words.ex: The workers built scaffolding around the building.
words.ex_cn: 工人们在大楼周围搭起了鹰架。
words.en: Scaffolding refers to a temporary structure on the outside of a building, made of wooden planks and metal poles, used by workers while building, repairing, or cleaning the building.

words.tr:
adj. 梯状的；分等级的；数量的；标量的
n. 标量；数量
words.ex: In physics, a scalar is a quantity that has magnitude but no direction.
words.ex_cn: 在物理学中，标量是一个只有大小而没有方向的量。
words.en: A scalar is a quantity that is fully described by a magnitude (or numerical value) alone.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.ex: He scratched his scalp because it was itchy.
words.ex_cn: 他挠头皮，因为那里发痒。
words.en: The skin covering the top of the human head, or a trophy taken by cutting off the scalp of an enemy.

words.ex: He scan the QR code with his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他用手机扫描了二维码。
words.en: To look at something carefully or quickly in order to find out specific information or to examine something thoroughly.

words.ex: The scandal made the news last week.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻上周上了新闻。
words.en: A scandal is a situation or event that is thought to be shocking and immoral and that everyone knows about.

words.tr: adj. 可耻的； 丢脸的；令人反感的；诽谤性的
words.ex: The scandalous news shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这则丑闻让每个人都震惊了。
words.en: If you describe something as scandalous, you are shocked that it is considered acceptable or that it happens.

words.tr:
adj. 斯堪的纳维亚（人）的；
n. 斯堪的纳维亚人（语）；
words.ex: He enjoys Scandinavian music and cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢斯堪的纳维亚音乐和寒冷的天气。
words.en: Relating to Scandinavia, its people, or their languages.

words.ex: He uses a scanner to copy documents.
words.ex_cn: 他使用扫描仪来复制文件。
words.en: A scanner is a device that captures images from photographic prints, posters, magazine pages, and similar sources for computer editing and display.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；欠缺的；微小的；
words.ex: There is scant evidence to support the claim.
words.ex_cn: 支持这一说法的证据不足。
words.en: If you describe something as scant, you mean that there is not enough of it or that it is not as much as it should be.

words.tr:
n. 替罪羊；代人受过者
v. 使…成为替罪羊
words.ex: He was made the scapegoat for the company's financial failures.
words.ex_cn: 他被当作公司财务失败的替罪羊。
words.en: A scapegoat is a person who is blamed for something that someone else has done.

words.ex: He has a scar on his arm from the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上有一道事故留下的伤疤。
words.en: A mark left on the skin after a wound or injury has healed, or the act of causing such a mark.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He scarcely ate anything at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐几乎没吃任何东西。
words.en: You use scarcely to emphasize that something is only just true or only just the case.

words.ex: The scarcity of water caused problems in the village.
words.ex_cn: 水的缺乏给村庄带来了问题。
words.en: A scarcity of something is a situation in which there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The loud noise scared the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something scares you, it frightens or worries you.

words.ex: She wore a warm scarf in winter.
words.ex_cn: 她在冬天戴了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: A scarf is a piece of cloth that you wear around your neck or head, usually to keep yourself warm.

words.tr: adj. 深红的；绯红的；猩红的；
words.ex: The scarlet leaves fell in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 深红色的叶子在秋天飘落。
words.en: A brilliant red color.

words.ex: The wind scatter the leaves everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得四处分散。
words.en: To scatter means to throw or drop things over a wide area in an irregular way, or to cause a group of people or animals to move apart in different directions.

words.ex: The scene at the park was peaceful.
words.ex_cn: 公园里的场景很宁静。
words.en: A scene is a part of a play or film in which the action stays in one place for a continuous period of time.

words.ex: The mountain scenery is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 山景非常美丽。
words.en: The natural features of a landscape considered in terms of their appearance, especially when picturesque.

words.ex: The scenic lake attracted many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 风景优美的湖泊吸引了许多游客。
words.en: Relating to or resembling scenery; picturesque.

words.tr: n. 香味；香水；气息；察觉；
words.ex: The flower has a sweet scent.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有甜美的香味。
words.en: A scent is a pleasant smell, especially one that is characteristic of a particular thing. It can also refer to the ability to detect smells or a clue or indication of something.

words.ex: He is skeptical about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新计划持怀疑态度。
words.en: If you are skeptical about something, you have doubts about it.

words.ex: His scepticism about the plan made him ask many questions.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划的怀疑态度让他提出了很多问题。
words.en: Scepticism is an attitude of doubting that particular claims or statements are true or that something will happen.

words.ex: I checked the class schedule for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我查看了明天的课程时间表。
words.en: A schedule is a plan that gives a list of events or tasks and the times at which each one should happen or be done.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: The scholar published a book about ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位学者出版了一本关于古代历史的书。
words.en: A scholar is a person who studies an academic subject and knows a lot about it.

words.ex: He won a scholarship to study at Harvard.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了一项去哈佛学习的奖学金。
words.en: A scholarship is a grant or payment made to support a student's education, awarded on the basis of academic or other achievement.

words.ex: My brother goes to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟每天早上上学。
words.en: A school is an institution where children are educated.

words.ex: The schoolboy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 那个小学生很快解出了这道数学题。
words.en: A schoolboy is a boy who attends school.

words.ex: The schoolchild walks to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个小学生每天早上步行去学校。
words.en: A schoolchild is a child who attends school.

words.ex: The schoolgirl walks to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个女学生每天早上步行去学校。
words.en: A schoolgirl is a girl who attends school.

words.ex: The schoolmaster was known for his strict discipline.
words.ex_cn: 这位男校长以严格的纪律著称。
words.en: A schoolmaster is a man who teaches in a school, especially a private school.

words.ex: The schoolmistress was known for her strict discipline.
words.ex_cn: 这位女校长以严格的纪律著称。
words.en: A schoolmistress is a woman who teaches in a school, especially a private school.

words.ex: He loves science and reads books about it.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢科学，经常读关于它的书。
words.en: Science is the study of the nature and behaviour of natural things and the knowledge that we obtain about them.

words.ex: He uses scientific methods to test his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用科学方法来测试他的想法。
words.en: Scientific means relating to science or using the methods of science.

words.ex: The scientist studies stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家研究夜空中的恒星。
words.en: A scientist is someone who has studied science and whose job is to teach or do research in science.

words.ex: She cut the paper with scissors.
words.ex_cn: 她用剪刀剪了纸。
words.en: Scissors are a tool used for cutting paper, cloth, hair, etc., consisting of two sharp blades fastened together in the middle so that the sharp edges slide against each other.

words.ex: My mom scolded me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈因为我回家晚而责备了我。
words.en: If you scold someone, you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He scooped soup with a spoon.
words.ex_cn: 他用勺子舀汤。
words.en: A scoop is a tool like a large spoon which is used for picking up substances such as ice cream or an amount of a substance that is held in a scoop. It can also refer to an important or exciting news story that is reported in a newspaper, magazine, or news broadcast before anyone else reports it.

words.tr: n. 滑板车；踏板车；小型摩托车
words.ex: He rides a scooter to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天骑滑板车去学校。
words.en: A scooter is a small motorcycle with a low seat. It is often used for short distances in urban areas.

words.ex: The scope of this project includes three cities.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的范围包括三个城市。
words.en: The range of one's perceptions, thoughts, or actions.

words.ex: The sun scorch the ground in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光灼烧地面。
words.en: To burn the surface of something so as to discolour or damage it.

words.tr: adj. 酷热的； v. “scorch”的现在分词；
words.ex: The scorching sun made the sand too hot to walk on.
words.ex_cn: 酷热的太阳使沙子热得无法赤脚行走。
words.en: If you describe the weather as scorching, you mean that it is extremely hot.

words.tr:
n. 分数；得分；总谱；乐谱；
v. 得分；
words.ex: He got a high score on the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中得了高分。
words.en: If you score a particular amount or number in a game or test, you achieve that amount or number.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.ex: The scorpion stung the boy.
words.ex_cn: 蝎子蜇了那个男孩。
words.en: A scorpion is a small creature which looks like a lobster and has a poisonous sting in its long tail.

words.ex: The police scotched the plan to rob the bank.
words.ex_cn: 警察阻止了抢劫银行的计划。
words.en: To scotch something means to stop it from continuing or developing.

words.ex: He lives in Scotland.
words.ex_cn: 他住在苏格兰。
words.en: Scotland is a country that is part of the United Kingdom, known for its distinct culture, history, and landscapes.

words.tr:
adj. 苏格兰（人）的；苏格兰英语的
n. 苏格兰人；苏格兰语
words.ex: He spoke in a strong Scots accent.
words.ex_cn: 他说话带有浓重的苏格兰口音。
words.en: Relating to Scotland, its people, or its language.

words.ex: The scotsman wears a kilt to the festival.
words.ex_cn: 这位苏格兰人穿着苏格兰短裙参加节日。
words.en: A Scotsman is a man who comes from Scotland.

words.ex: The Scotswoman was known for her traditional tartan dress.
words.ex_cn: 这位苏格兰女人以其传统的格子裙装而闻名。
words.en: A woman who is a native or inhabitant of Scotland.

words.tr: adj. 苏格兰的；苏格兰人的；
words.ex: He wears a Scottish kilt on St. Andrew's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他在圣安德鲁日穿苏格兰短裙。
words.en: Of or relating to Scotland, its people, or its language.

words.ex: He is a scoundrel who lies to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个对所有人都撒谎的无赖。
words.en: A scoundrel is someone who behaves in a dishonest or unfair way.

words.ex: She scoured the pan until it was clean.
words.ex_cn: 她把锅擦得干干净净。
words.en: If you scour something, you clean it by rubbing it hard with something rough.

words.tr:
n. 侦察兵；
v. 搜寻；
words.ex: The scout watched the enemy's movement quietly.
words.ex_cn: 侦察兵悄悄观察敌人的动向。
words.en: A scout is someone who is sent to an area of countryside to find out the position of an enemy or to search for a suitable place for a military camp.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.tr:
n. 小块；碎片；废金属；吵架
v. 废弃；取消
adj. 废弃的
words.ex: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一张纸片。
words.en: A scrap is a small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over after the greater part has been used. It can also mean to discard or get rid of something as being no longer useful or necessary.

words.tr:
v. 刮；擦；刮出刺耳声；勉强通过
n. 刮；擦；擦痕；刮擦声
words.ex: He scraped his knee on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 他在粗糙的地面上擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: To remove something from a surface using a sharp or rough edge, or to injure a part of the body by rubbing it against a rough surface.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: The child screamed when she saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当那个孩子看到狗时，她尖叫了起来。
words.en: If you scream, you shout or cry in a loud high-pitched voice, usually because you are in pain or are very frightened.

words.tr:
n. 屏幕；屏风；掩蔽物；
v. 筛查；掩蔽；
words.ex: The movie is playing on the screen.
words.ex_cn: 电影正在屏幕上播放。
words.en: A screen is a flat surface on which pictures or words are shown, such as the one on a television or computer. It can also refer to a partition used to divide or protect an area. As a verb, to screen means to examine something in order to decide whether it is suitable for a particular purpose, or to protect someone or something from something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: He spent months writing the screenplay for the film.
words.ex_cn: 他为这部电影花了数月时间撰写剧本。
words.en: A screenplay is the script of a movie, including the dialogue and the instructions for the actors and director.

words.tr:
n. 螺丝钉；
v. 拧紧；
words.ex: He tightened the screw with a screwdriver.
words.ex_cn: 他用螺丝刀拧紧了螺丝钉。
words.en: A screw is a metal object similar to a nail, with a raised spiral line around it. Screws are used to fasten things together.

words.tr: n. 螺丝刀；改锥；螺丝起子；伏特加橙汁鸡尾酒
words.ex: He used a screwdriver to tighten the loose screws.
words.ex_cn: 他用螺丝刀拧紧了松动的螺丝。
words.en: A screwdriver is a tool that is used for turning screws. It has a handle and a long metal part that fits into the top of the screw.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；匆匆地写；乱涂乱画
n. 潦草的字迹；涂鸦
words.ex: He scribbled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了名字。
words.en: To scribble means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly.

words.ex: He wrote a script for a short movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部短片写了剧本。
words.en: A script is the written form of a play, film, or broadcast. It includes the dialogue and stage directions.

words.tr: n. （电影、电视剧、广播剧的）剧作家；
words.ex: The scriptwriter wrote a funny TV show.
words.ex_cn: 这位剧作家写了一部搞笑的电视剧。
words.en: A scriptwriter is a person who writes scripts, especially for films, television, or radio.

words.tr:
n. 卷轴；
v. 卷动；
words.ex: He unrolled the ancient scroll.
words.ex_cn: 他展开了一卷古老的卷轴。
words.en: A scroll is a roll of paper or parchment with writing or pictures on it. As a verb, to scroll means to move displayed text or graphics on a screen in a particular direction in order to view different parts of them.

words.ex: The deer walked through the scrub near the hill.
words.ex_cn: 鹿穿过了山边的灌木丛。
words.en: To scrub something means to rub it hard in order to clean it, especially using a stiff brush and water.

words.tr: n. 仔细研究；详细检查；
words.ex: The teacher examined the student's work under close scrutiny.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作业进行了仔细研究。
words.en: If someone or something is under scrutiny, they are being studied or observed very carefully.

words.ex: The sculptor carved a statue from stone.
words.ex_cn: 这位雕刻家从石头中雕刻出一座雕像。
words.en: A sculptor is an artist who creates sculptures.

words.tr: n. 雕刻（术）；雕塑品；雕刻品；
words.ex: He made a beautiful sculpture from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土做了一件精美的雕刻。
words.en: Sculpture is the art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving stone or wood or by casting metal or plaster.

words.tr:
n. 长柄大镰刀
v. 用长柄大镰刀割
words.ex: The farmer swings the scythe to cut grass.
words.ex_cn: 农夫挥动镰刀割草。
words.en: A scythe is a tool with a long curved blade at right angles to a long handle, used for cutting grass, grain, or other crops.

words.ex: The fish swim in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在海里游泳。
words.en: The sea is the salty water that covers about three-quarters of the Earth's surface.

words.tr: n. 海产食物（如海鱼、贝类等）；
words.ex: We ate fresh seafood at the seaside restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在海边的餐厅吃了新鲜的海产食物。
words.en: Seafood refers to fish and shellfish from the sea that are eaten as food.

words.ex: The seagull flew over the beach.
words.ex_cn: 海鸥飞过了海滩。
words.en: A seagull is a common coastal bird that is known for its loud call and its habit of scavenging for food.

words.ex: He sealed the envelope with glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用胶水把信封封上了。
words.en: A seal is a device or substance that is used to close off or fasten an opening or container, making it airtight or watertight. It can also refer to a marine mammal with flippers for swimming.

words.tr:
n. 接缝；缝合处；矿层；煤层
v. 缝合；有裂痕
words.ex: The seam of the shirt came loose.
words.ex_cn: 衬衫的接缝松开了。
words.en: A seam is a line where two pieces of fabric are sewn together in a garment or other article.

words.ex: The seaman sailed the boat across the sea.
words.ex_cn: 水手驾船横渡大海。
words.en: A seaman is a sailor, especially one who is not an officer.

words.tr: n. 海港；港口；港口城市
words.ex: The seaport was bustling with activity as ships were loading and unloading cargo.
words.ex_cn: 海港里船只正在装卸货物，一片繁忙的景象。
words.en: A seaport is a town or city with a harbor where ships load and unload.

words.tr:
n. 探究；搜索；
v. 搜索；搜寻；
words.ex: The search for truth took many years.
words.ex_cn: 对真理的探究花了多年时间。
words.en: If you search for something or someone, you look carefully for them because you want to find them.

words.ex: He found a seashell on the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上发现了一个贝壳。
words.en: A seashell is the empty shell of a small sea creature, often found on beaches.

words.ex: Children play near the seashore.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在海岸边玩耍。
words.en: The land along the edge of the sea or ocean, especially the part that is between the land and the water.

words.ex: He felt seasick on the boat.
words.ex_cn: 他在船上感到晕船。
words.en: If someone is seasick, they feel sick because of the movement of the boat they are on.

words.ex: He felt seasickness on the boat.
words.ex_cn: 他在船上感到晕船。
words.en: Nausea and dizziness caused by the motion of a ship at sea.

words.ex: We walked along the seaside at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 我们在日落时沿着海边散步。
words.en: The area by the sea, especially a beach area where people go for holidays.

words.ex: Spring is a beautiful season.
words.ex_cn: 春天是一个美丽的季节。
words.en: A season is one of the four periods of the year: spring, summer, autumn, or winter. It can also refer to a period of the year characterized by particular conditions of weather, temperature, etc., or a period of the year when a particular sport is played.

words.tr:
n. 调味品；佐料
v. 给 ... 调味；适应；风干；“season”的现在分词
words.ex: She added seasoning to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 她给汤里加了调味料。
words.en: Seasoning is a substance that is added to food to improve its flavor.

words.tr:
n. 座位；
v. 使坐下；
words.ex: Please take your seat before the class starts.
words.ex_cn: 上课前请坐好你的座位。
words.en: A seat is an object that you can sit on, for example a chair.

words.ex: He always wears his seatbelt when he drives.
words.ex_cn: 他开车时总是系安全带。
words.en: A seatbelt is a strap that you fasten across your body when you are in a vehicle, to prevent you from being thrown out or injured in an accident.

words.tr:
adj. 向海的；朝海的
adv. 向海；向海那一边
words.ex: The boat moved seaward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 船慢慢地向海的方向驶去。
words.en: Towards the sea.

words.ex: The fish swim among the seaweed near the shore.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在岸边的海藻间游动。
words.en: Seaweed is a plant that grows in the sea, especially in the ocean. It is often used in food, medicine, and cosmetics.

words.tr:
adj. 第二的；
n. 第二；秒；片刻；
adv. 第二；
words.ex: He got the second prize in the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中获得了第二名。
words.en: Second is used to describe something that is next after the first in order, rank, importance, or occurrence.

words.tr: adj. 中等的；次要的；第二的；
words.ex: He attends a secondary school in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城里上一所中学。
words.en: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.

words.ex: He bought a secondhand bike for $50.
words.ex_cn: 他花50美元买了一辆二手自行车。
words.en: Something that is secondhand is not new and has been owned by someone else before.

words.tr: adj. 二流的；平庸的；不是优秀的
words.ex: The movie was second-rate, lacking in both plot and character development.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，故事情节和人物塑造都很欠缺。
words.en: If you describe something as second-rate, you mean that it is of poor quality.

words.ex: The government kept the mission in secrecy.
words.ex_cn: 政府将这次任务保密。
words.en: Secrecy is the practice of keeping something secret, or the state of being secret.

words.tr:
n. 秘密；
adj. 秘密的；
words.ex: He kept the secret from everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他把秘密藏了起来，谁也没告诉。
words.en: If something is secret, it is known about by only a small number of people, and is not told or shown to anyone else.

words.ex: He works in a secretarial role at the office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室担任秘书工作。
words.en: Relating to the work of a secretary or the duties of a secretary.

words.tr: n. 秘书处；书记处；秘书（书记，部长等）的职位
words.ex: The secretariat sends out meeting notices every week.
words.ex_cn: 秘书处每周发送会议通知。
words.en: The administrative department of an organization, especially a large political organization, that is responsible for its day-to-day running.

words.ex: The secretary types letters for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 秘书为经理打字。
words.en: A secretary is a person whose job is to do office work, such as typing letters, answering phone calls, and arranging meetings.

words.ex: The sect held unusual beliefs that differed from the main religion.
words.ex_cn: 这个派别的信仰与主流宗教不同。
words.en: A sect is a group of people who have different religious beliefs from other people in the same religion.

words.ex: This book has five sections.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有五个部分。
words.en: A section of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: The health sector needs more funding.
words.ex_cn: 医疗部门需要更多资金。
words.en: A particular area of activity, especially one that is part of a larger area of activity or one that is considered separately from other areas.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 安全；保障；防护措施；
words.ex: The school improved security to protect students.
words.ex_cn: 学校加强了安全措施以保护学生。
words.en: Security refers to the state of being free from danger or threat, or measures taken to ensure safety.

words.ex: Rivers carry sediment to the sea.
words.ex_cn: 河流把沉积物带到大海。
words.en: Material that settles to the bottom of a liquid; matter that has been deposited by some natural process.

words.ex: I see a bird in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 我看到树上有一只鸟。
words.en: to perceive with the eyes; to understand or comprehend something

words.tr:
n. 种子；籽；
v. 播种；
words.ex: The farmer planted the seed in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫把种子种在土里。
words.en: A seed is the small, hard part of a plant from which a new plant grows.

words.ex: The gardener planted a seedling in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在花园里种了一株幼苗。
words.en: A seedling is a young plant that has grown from a seed.

words.ex: He seeks help when he is stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当他遇到困难时，他会寻求帮助。
words.en: If you seek something, you try to find it or obtain it.

words.ex: He seems tired after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后似乎很累。
words.en: If something seems to be a particular way, it appears to be that way.

words.tr: adv. 似乎；看似；表面上看；
words.ex: He is seemingly calm, but he is nervous inside.
words.ex_cn: 他似乎很平静，但内心很紧张。
words.en: appearing to be true or real but not necessarily so

words.ex: The children played on the seesaw at the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里玩跷跷板。
words.en: A seesaw is a long board which is balanced on a fixed part in the middle so that when one end goes up, the other goes down. It is used especially by children to play on.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: The boy tried to seize the ball.
words.ex_cn: 男孩试图抓住球。
words.en: If you seize something, you take hold of it quickly, firmly, and forcefully.

words.tr: n. 夺取；占有；强占；（疾病）发作
words.ex: The seizure of the city ended the war.
words.ex_cn: 对这座城市的夺取结束了战争。
words.en: A seizure is the act of taking something by force or with legal authority, or a sudden attack of an illness, especially one that affects the brain.

words.ex: He seldom eats fast food.
words.ex_cn: 他很少吃快餐。
words.en: If something seldom happens, it happens only occasionally.

words.tr:
v. 选择；挑选；
adj. 精心挑选的；
words.ex: He will select the best candidate for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他将选择最适合这份工作的人。
words.en: If you select something, you choose it from a number of things of the same kind.

words.ex: The selection of books was very good.
words.ex_cn: 书籍的选择非常好。
words.en: The act of carefully choosing someone or something as the best or most suitable.

words.tr: adj. 选择性的；精挑细选的；
words.ex: He is selective about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you are selective, you choose things carefully, for example, the things that you buy or do.

words.ex: He learned to love his self.
words.ex_cn: 他学会了爱自己。
words.en: Your self is your basic personality or nature, especially considered in terms of what you are really like as a person.

words.ex: She is self-assured when she speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 她在全班面前讲话时很自信。
words.en: Someone who is self-assured shows confidence in what they say and do because they are sure of their own abilities.

words.ex: He has self-confidence when he speaks in public.
words.ex_cn: 他当众讲话时很有自信。
words.en: Self-confidence is the belief in one's own abilities and judgment.

words.tr: adj. 不自然的；忸怩的；难为情的
words.ex: He felt self-conscious when speaking in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时感到不自然。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as self-conscious, you mean that they are strongly aware of who or what they are.

words.tr: adj. 完备的；设施独立的；独立自足的；沉默寡言的
words.ex: The cabin is self-contained with its own water and electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这个小屋是自给自足的，有自己独立的水和电。
words.en: A self-contained place or thing is complete and does not need other things to function or exist.

words.ex: His story is self-contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事自相矛盾。
words.en: If you say that something is self-contradictory, you mean that it contains two statements or beliefs that cannot both be true.

words.tr: n. 自我控制；克己； 自控力
words.ex: He showed self-control when he stayed calm.
words.ex_cn: 当他保持冷静时，他表现出了自制力。
words.en: Self-control is the ability to not show your feelings or not do the things that your feelings make you want to do.

words.ex: He feels self-criticism after making a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他犯错后感到自我批评。
words.en: Self-criticism is the act of pointing out one's own faults and shortcomings.

words.ex: The principle of self-determination is enshrined in the United Nations Charter.
words.ex_cn: 民族自决的原则被载入联合国宪章。
words.en: Self-determination is the ability or right of a country or a person to make their own decisions about how they should be governed or how they should live.

words.ex: He learns English through self-education.
words.ex_cn: 他通过自学学习英语。
words.en: Self-education refers to the process of acquiring knowledge or skills by one's own efforts rather than through formal instruction or schooling.

words.tr: adj. 自己经营的；个体经营的；非受雇于人的
words.ex: He is self-employed and works from home.
words.ex_cn: 他是自由职业者，在家工作。
words.en: Someone who is self-employed works for themselves rather than for an employer.

words.tr: adj. 不证自明的；不言而喻的
words.ex: It is self-evident that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾是显而易见的。
words.en: Something that is self-evident is so obvious that there is no need for proof or explanation.

words.tr: n. 自治；政治独立；自制；克己
words.ex: The island wants self-government.
words.ex_cn: 这个岛屿想要自治。
words.en: Self-government is the ability or right of a country, region, or organization to govern itself independently of external control.

words.ex: He acted out of self-interest, not care for others.
words.ex_cn: 他出于私利行事，而不是关心他人。
words.en: Self-interest is the act of considering one's own advantage and well-being over others.

words.ex: He is selfish and never shares his toys.
words.ex_cn: 他很自私，从不分享他的玩具。
words.en: If you say that someone is selfish, you mean that they only care about their own interests and do not consider the needs or feelings of other people.

words.ex: She is selfless and always helps others.
words.ex_cn: 她很无私，总是帮助别人。
words.en: If you say that someone is selfless, you approve of them because they care about other people more than themselves.

words.ex: She felt a wave of self-pity wash over her.
words.ex_cn: 她感到一阵自怜涌上心头。
words.en: Self-pity is a feeling of sadness for yourself because you believe you have suffered so much.

words.tr: adj. 自立的；靠自己力量的
words.ex: He is self-reliant and solves his problems alone.
words.ex_cn: 他自立，自己解决自己的问题。
words.en: Someone who is self-reliant is capable of doing things and making decisions by themselves, without needing other people to help them.

words.ex: He lost his self-respect after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友撒谎后失去了自尊。
words.en: Self-respect is a feeling of confidence and pride in your own ability and worth.

words.tr: adj. 自我服务的；自助的
words.ex: The restaurant has a self-service buffet.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅有一个自助餐台。
words.en: A self-service system or place is one where you can serve yourself, rather than being served by someone else.

words.ex: He wants to be self-sufficient by growing his own food.
words.ex_cn: 他想通过自己种食物来实现自给自足。
words.en: A self-sufficient person or thing is able to provide for themselves without outside assistance.
